  1. Requirements definition
  2. REQ-F70-EU-IC-03

Cockpit lighting without reflections in the mirrors and windscreen

Proposal
1, implement. Instrument panel complaints (33 rows, 11 defects) include repeated reports that dash and ambient lights reflect in the door mirrors and windscreen at night, which owners call a safety issue.
Horizon
H1. Light guide and default brightness changes.
Domain
Interior Comfort & Materials
Markets
EU
Evidence level
B (the best level of the primary and supporting findings)
Status
proposed, version 1

Statement

Ambient and display lighting shall not reflect in the side mirrors, side windows or windscreen at night at any brightness setting.

Acceptance criteria

One row per market where expectations differ. Basis: evidence is a measured study value or a count; assumption is the agent's proposal for the product manager to set.

MarketMetricTargetHow measuredBasis
EUVisible reflection of interior lighting in the side mirrors at nightNone at default brightnessNight visibility testassumption

    • parking the car is really a pain, the camera view and the sensors dont match up properly and the beeping noise is distracting. there are no usb ports, just a phone charger. the seating isnt that comfortable either. the dashboard is also distracting, with the radio showing no channel list, only a bunch of colourful icons.

      F70-1545 · Source A · GB · ICE · Defect, Instrument panel, Malfunction · F70_feedback_hackathon.xlsx, row 2,982

    • the 120i is a lovely car, nice styling and shape. i'm not completely convinced about how easy it is to get to some things with the new dash layout, although i am 73 and slower than younger people who are up to date with modern tech. my main concern is what i feel is a design fault in the interior lighting: the side pods at each corner of the dash reflect into the wing mirrors at night and really cut down what you can see. i think this is not just a design issue but a safety one as well. kind regards mr a carson

      F70-1612 · Source A · GB · ICE · Defect, Instrument panel, Damage · F70_feedback_hackathon.xlsx, row 3,119

    • generally the car is good, but in my view the electronic dash totally spoils it. my wife and i have done around 3800 miles since buying it and we have decided that trying to change anything hidden in the dash while on the move is just too dangerous, because of how long your eyes are off the road. so if we are together the passenger does the adjustments, and if alone we pull over to change things. i feel this system is many times more complex than my iphone, and it is illegal to use an iphone while driving. what is wrong with simple knobs, switches and dials? i also dread to think what it will cost to replace the dash when it eventually fails.

      F70-1846 · Source A · GB · ICE · Defect, Instrument panel, Damage · F70_feedback_hackathon.xlsx, row 3,546

    • as a small car it is excellent overall. plenty of space, comfortable and quick off the mark, with very smooth pull through the gears and really strong grip and cornering behaviour. the keyless boot release can be a bit unreliable. the digital key setup can also be frustrating at times: with my iphone and apple watch the car unlocks as i walk up, but if i open the boot to load it, by the time i've shut it and gone round to the driver door it has locked again and i need to stand for a moment until it opens. the mirrors do not always fold when locking, and the instrument cluster sometimes drops my personal layout. aside from those small digital issues, everything else is perfect.

      F70-0955 · Source A · GB · ICE · Defect, Instrument panel, Malfunction · F70_feedback_hackathon.xlsx, row 1,864

    • fantastic car but extremely disappointed that after only about 5 weeks with a brand new model the whole dashboard crashed and needed a new part, meaning we were without our own car for roughly another 5 weeks! (the dealer in portstewart did give us a replacement car) but our main issue is with bmw for this kind of failure on a new car! it really knocks our confidence in bmw going forward and it was embarrassing having to tell people our car had to go back to the garage for repairs!! definitely not good for bmw. it is frustrating that bmw uk do not see this as a major problem and were hesitant to even admit it was disruptive for customers, so although the dealer gave us a hotel voucher it would have been considerate for bmw to at least acknowledge the fault and give an explanation!
